To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antigenic variation among murid coronaviruses occurs on the peplomeric glycoprotein E2 and that there are four antigenic sites, A(E2), B(E2), C(E2) and E(E2) on E2.

the E2 glycopeptides of six murine coronaviruse strains were antigenically polymorphic, and that the antigenic sites on E2 glycoprotein were highly conserved among the strains of the same serogroup, but differed between serogroups.

antigenic determinants on the peplomers of murine coronaviuses can be classified into four categories: 1) highly conserved determinants that are present on all strains, 2) conserved determinants present on some strains, 3) polymorphic determinants present on only one strain, and 4) polymorphic determinats present on only some strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antigenic structure of the murine coronaviridae.
the development of a panel of MAb to study the antigenic relationships of murine coronoviruses.
the identification of the E2 antigenic determinants and their distribution on the six MHV strains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E1 and N proteins of murine coronavi- rus are highly conserved, while the E2 glyco- protein is highly polymorphic.
the antigenic sites of the E2 glyco-protein vary in their degree of polymorphism, ranging from the conserved site A(E2) to the highly polymorphic site D(E2).
MHV-4, MHV-3 and MHV-1 are closely antigenically related, but are distinguishable by the presence of antigenic site C(E2).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MHV strains differ antigenically on the basis of the E2 glycopeptide, but that the antigenic determinants on E2 are not necessarily associated with differences in pathogenicity.
the MHV-4 E2 antigen is highly polymorphic and that the antigenic sites are located at topographically distinct sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the E2 protein is the most variable of the three major structural proteins of murid coronaviruses.
there appears to be a high degree of antigenic conservation among the structural proteins of the murine coronavirinae.
the E2 glyco protein is the major antigenic target for neutralizing antibodies.
